evidence: Plan item 4.4 (docs/AGENT_PLAN.md, phase 4: diffuse order between cells). The modulation engines tested single wavevectors only -- each zone-boundary point and the strongest general modes, each against a family-wise bar -- so short-range order between cells, which spreads its power over many q (a diffuse sheet, rod or hump) with no single mode near the bar, went unseen. Parseval fixes the mean power over q != 0 (N/(N - 1), each site's mean subtracted), so a test can only be about how the power is spread, never its total. The statistic: over the compared modes (one per +q/-q pair, no long wave, no zone-boundary point, none the general test found ordered), the normal scores of the ranks of the element's power are regressed on the templates cos(2 pi q.R) of the 13 neighbour-cell lags R (the 26 cells around a cell, one of each +R/-R pair; correlation Gamma(R) between a site's displacements in cells R apart adds 2 Gamma(R) cos(2 pi q.R) to the power over its mean), chi2 = (K - 1) |P a|^2 / |a|^2 with r degrees of freedom (the lags the grid resolves); under independent cells (F1's null) the power at every such q is identically distributed, so the ranks are exchangeable and the statistic is chi2_r whatever the cells hold. Sidak over every element (as F3). Effect size: the strongest neighbour-cell correlation |Gamma(R)| from the least-squares fit of the power, at least 0.1 (a +-20 % modulation of the power across q). Long waves (every |q_i| <= 0.25) stay out: RMC's box-scale waves are the longWave finding, not short-range order. Zone-boundary points stay out: they are real Fourier sums, tested one by one. A model-based variant (the raw power against F1's null variance) was anti-conservative on shared-variable families (11 against 4.6 expected at 2 sigma over 200 two-feature configurations, its chi2 variance inflated by the power's fourth cumulant); ranks bound what any one q adds, so one mode, however strong, cannot make the test (its chi2 is unchanged when the strongest mode is made a million times stronger). Calibration (1,000 configurations per family, Python engines; diffuse sigma at 3 / 2 / 1 sigma against 1.35 / 22.8 / 158.7 expected per 1,000): thermal 0 / 12 / 147, Jahn-Teller 0 / 16 / 119, two-feature 0 / 13 / 114, octahedral 2 / 23 / 137, breathing 0 / 20 / 149, rigid dimers 0 / 16 / 165 (pooled at 3 sigma 2/6000 = 0.03 %, Clopper-Pearson 95 % [0.00, 0.12]); 5,000 octahedral configurations: 6 (0.12 %, [0.04, 0.26]); 5,000 two-feature configurations: 0; the DEV generator kinds (JS engines) 3 diffuse verdicts in 7,000 configurations (0.04 %). Known answers: B displacements correlated between neighbouring cells along a, u(c) = e(c) - 0.3 (e(c + a) + e(c - a)) over the perovskite's thermal motion (neighbour correlation -0.27, the power on the whole sheet q_a = 1/2): found in all 100 configurations (in antiphase along [1 0 0], estimate -0.34 +- 0.14), with no cell doubling and no general order in the known-answer configuration; in phase along c (+0.27): 100/100 (+0.25 +- 0.06); at -0.19, 74/100; at -0.10, 4/100. One strong mode alone is not diffuse order: dev-zone-boundary's Ti doubling (18.9 sigma) leaves the diffuse test at -3.1 sigma, a planted doubling (B +-0.1 A) reads as diffuse order in 0 of 100 configurations, the weak order in 0 of 100, and an ordered general mode is left out of the test. No dev case reads as diffuse order. The Demo (GaTa4Se8, RMC, 250 K): its three elements are correlated in phase between neighbouring cells beyond the long waves (5.8, 13.4 and 9.1 sigma; correlations +0.13, +0.22, +0.11, isotropic, all positive and decaying with the lag): the smooth correlated motion RMC's box-scale waves extend to, which the tool says as neighbouring cells moving together, not a superstructure; the GaNb4Se8 5 K run's are below the effect bar (+0.05 to +0.09 at 3.1-3.7 sigma). What it adds to the zone-boundary and general tests: a pattern of many q each far below the per-mode bars (ratio 3, 3 sigma over every compared mode), at one test per element. Arms A and A+ on dev before and after: A+ does not read diffuseOrder (no feature kind; adding one changes the scoring, the user's call), and the only moved record is F1's (2026-10-19-modulation-null). Approved by the manager on the user's delegation, 2026-10-19.
proposed_fix: Both engines (rmc_toolkits/modulations.py diffuse_order and _diffuse_finding; workers/modulations.js diffuseOrder and its finding; constants mirrored: DIFFUSE_LAGS, DIFFUSE_SIGMA = 3, DIFFUSE_CORRELATION = 0.1, DIFFUSE_MODES_PER_TERM = 2, DIFFUSE_RANK_RTOL = 1e-9, DIFFUSE_PHASES) give each element `diffuse` = {modes, df, chiSquare, sigma, correlations (Gamma per lag), lag, correlation, phase} and `verdict.diffuseOrder` = {answer, because, evidence: [one Evidence record in the cluster engine's form: statistic neighbourCellCorrelation, against independentCells, observed = |Gamma| of the strongest lag, null 0, z = the family-wise sigma, change, bar {z: 3, change: 0.1}, side above, clears = evidence_clears(record)]}; answer = clears; because correlated_in_phase / correlated_antiphase / below_correlation / below_sigma / undefined_statistic / too_few_modes (fewer than 2 compared modes per term: a 4 x 4 x 4 grid) / no_displacements. The payload's family gains `diffuse` (the elements), rules gain the constants. The parity fixture pins it (two planted cases added; the generator refuses a decided statistic within 1e-6 of its bar and any rank tie, lag resolution or strongest-lag tie near its tolerance). analyze_modulations shows a `diffuse` row [lag, correlation, sigma] per element (F2's rule on the correlation's bar), explains it in its note, says antiphase correlation per element as short-range order between cells and in-phase correlation for every element in one note (neighbouring cells moving together, as RMC's long waves and acoustic-like thermal motion give, not a superstructure); its dataShape declares the row and its result budget is 4,500 characters. facts.modulation gains no field: the answer audit (src/llm/copilot) has no rule that would read it. Arm A+ reads cellDoubling, generalOrder and longWave only. Commits 82801fe (engines) and 6305217 (tool, arms, protocol 2026-10-19.16). Approved by the manager on the user's delegation, 2026-10-19.
